nodes.title: G-valued global lifting datum
nodes.statement: A lifting datum consists of a global field F of characteristic different from p, a finite set S of finite places containing all residual ramification and all places above p in characteristic zero, a finite extension E/Q_p with integers O, uniformizer ϖ and residue field k, a smooth affine O-group G with split reductive G⁰ and finite étale component group of order prime to p, a continuous ρ̄:Γ_{F,S}→G(k), and a continuous lift μ:Γ_{F,S}→(G/G^der)(O) of its quotient. Here G^der is the derived group of G⁰. Require p odd and very good and the central isogeny G^der×Z⁰_{G⁰}→G⁰ to have prime-to-p kernel. Write M=Lie(G^der)_k with action Ad∘ρ̄ and M*=Hom_k(M,k)(1); * includes exactly one cyclotomic twist. Lift^μ(A) is the existing fixed-quotient continuous lifting functor, with strict conjugacy by the congruence kernel when passing to deformation classes.
hypotheses: The finite component action and μ are part of the data; the quotient G/G^der need not be a torus.
In characteristic zero μ is de Rham for geometric conclusions.
proofSteps: Specialize the existing G-valued framed functor, then impose equality of the quotient representation.
Use the prime-to-p central isogeny to identify its infinitesimal kernel with Lie(G^der).
Use the invariant trace form only under the prime hypotheses to identify M∨ with M; keep its Tate twist visible.
acceptance: For GL₂ and p odd, fixed multiplier is fixed determinant and M=sl₂(k), of dimension 3.

nodes.title: Odd G-valued residual representations

At a real place this is the fixed space of ρ̄(c_v). For nontrivial semisimple G this condition rules out complex places. For a torus both dimensions are zero, so total reality is a separate hypothesis in the geometric theorem.
hypotheses: Use the standing good-characteristic conditions and the actual component containing complex conjugation.
For a torus the numerical condition alone does not force F totally real; record total reality separately in geometric lifting theorems.
proofSteps: Use involution eigenspaces in the adjoint module and the root decomposition to prove the lower bound.
Compare the definition with the matrix determinant test for GL₂.

nodes.title: The four residual-image conditions
nodes.statement: For a lifting datum put K=F(ρ̄,μ_p), F̃ the extension cut out by the component map, and K∞=K(μ_{p∞}). Define C1 by H⁰(Γ_F,M)=0, C2 by H⁰(Γ_F,M*)=0, C3 by: no nonzero F_p[Γ_F]-quotient of M is isomorphic to an F_p[Γ_F]-subquotient of M*, and C4 by H¹(Gal(K/F),M*)=0. The package C1,C3 is Assumption 4.1; C4 is Assumption 3.1; C2 and the specified local lifts supply Assumption 5.1. Define D_cyc=max{d:μ_{p^d}⊂K}, with d≥1.
hypotheses: Prime-field modules are used in C3 even when k is larger than F_p.
K uses the full residual representation, not merely its adjoint image.
proofSteps: Reuse the arithmetic invariant and cohomology carriers.
State quotient/subquotient nonoverlap as a property of genuine equivariant maps; exclude the zero quotient.
Take fixed fields of the finite representations and cyclotomic character.
acceptance: M=0 satisfies C1–C4; C3 does not fail on W=0.

sources.match: The source isolates the four independent hypotheses that replace residual irreducibility.

At such a place M and M* have trivial residual action; values of H¹ classes on σ_w and τ_w are independent of changing a cocycle by a coboundary.

Norm and Frobenius conventions agree in both characteristics.
proofSteps: Interpret triviality as complete splitting in K.
Use the existing local tame-quotient description and the vanishing of coboundaries for trivial action.
acceptance: A place split in F(ρ̄) with q_w not congruent to 1 mod p is not trivial.

nodes.title: Cocycle fields and strong linear disjointness
nodes.statement: If the finite Γ_F-module V is trivial over K and z∈H¹(Γ_F,V), define K_z/K by the kernel of the homomorphism z|Γ_K. Its Galois group is the actual additive image z(Γ_K), with Gal(K/F) acting by conjugation. A finite family {L_i/K} is strongly linearly disjoint when the restriction Gal(∏L_i/K)→∏Gal(L_i/K) is an isomorphism; an infinite family has this property for every finite subfamily. Over K, classes and cocycles yield the same field.
hypotheses: All fields sit in one fixed separable closure and are Galois over F where conjugation is used.
proofSteps: Use the kernel of restriction on the existing continuous cocycle carrier.
Compare changing representatives and prove equivariance directly from the cocycle identity.
Express strong disjointness by the restriction isomorphism, not just pairwise intersections.
acceptance: The zero class cuts out K itself.

sources.locator: §1.3, pp.7–8; Lemma 3.7, pp.15–16; FKP19 Notation 5.1, pp.25–26
sources.match: The proof uses cocycle images and disjointness of entire finite families.

nodes.title: Trivial conjugation on an abelian compositum
nodes.statement: For finite Galois L/F and abelian A/F, conjugation by Gal(L/F) on Gal(LA/L), defined by lifting to Gal(LA/F), is trivial.
proofSteps: Restriction embeds Gal(LA/L) into the abelian group Gal(A/F).
Every commutator restricts to the identity on A and on L, hence on LA.
acceptance: For two distinct quadratic extensions of Q, their biquadratic compositum has trivial conjugation on either relative C₂ factor.

sources.match: This elementary field lemma is the input excluding nontrivial residual constituents from cyclotomic intersections.

nodes.title: The first cyclotomic layer in a cocycle field
nodes.statement: For a finite Galois K/F containing μ_p, D_cyc is finite and Gal(K∞/K)≅Z_p. If V is killed by p and trivial on Γ_K, then K_z∩K∞ is either K or the unique degree-p layer K(μ_{p^{D_cyc+1}}). If its Γ_F/K conjugation action has no nonzero trivial quotient, the intersection is K. These assertions also hold for global function fields with p different from the characteristic.
hypotheses: p is odd; the roots of unity in K are finite.
proofSteps: Use the structure of the p-adic cyclotomic image; over a function field use its constant-field description.
Gal(K_z/K) is killed by p, so any procyclic quotient has order at most p.
Apply trivial conjugation in an abelian compositum.
acceptance: If V=F_p with trivial conjugation, its cocycle field may be the first degree-p cyclotomic layer; absence of nontrivial constituents cannot be replaced by absence of submodules.

sources.match: Only the first degree-p cyclotomic layer can obstruct unrestricted norm prescriptions.

nodes.title: Absolutely irreducible reductive images
nodes.statement: For a connected split reductive G/k and an absolutely G-irreducible finite subgroup Γ⊂G(k), p>2(dim Lie(G^der)+1) implies semisimplicity of Lie(G^der), absence of a nontrivial normal p-subgroup of Γ, and H¹(Γ,Lie(G^der)⊗χ)=0 for every character χ. For p>5, excluding p∣n+1 in type A_n, H⁰(Γ,Lie(G^der))=0. Absolute G-irreducibility means noncontainment in every proper parabolic after extension to k̄.
hypotheses: The module and character may be considered after a finite splitting extension of k.
proofSteps: Use low-height complete reducibility for the adjoint representation.
A normal p-subgroup fixes every simple constituent, hence lies in the prime-to-p center.
Apply the requested small-representation H¹ theorem to the adjoint image.
For invariants split a fixed Lie element into its semisimple and nilpotent parts and use the proper-parabolic centralizer criteria.
acceptance: For SL₂ at p≥7 a full SL₂(F_p) image has no fixed vector in sl₂; absolute irreducibility refers to parabolics of SL₂ rather than an arbitrary faithful representation.

sources.match: These are the finite-image prerequisites from the earlier paper, including the bounds and centralizer argument.

nodes.title: Bounded cyclic quotients of irreducible images
nodes.statement: For a fixed split semisimple root datum and sufficiently large p there is a_G such that every absolutely G-irreducible Γ⊂G(k) has no cyclic quotient of order at least a_G. In the adjoint case there is also n_G, depending only on the root datum, such that for each semisimple s some s^n, n∣n_G, has Levi centralizer. The semisimple version follows from the adjoint one with the bounded central kernel accounted for.
hypotheses: The constants are uniform in finite k of characteristic p; a prime bound is part of the conclusion.
proofSteps: Use the Larsen–Pink normal series, with its central prime-to-p part when O_p(Γ)=1.
A large cyclic quotient forces a large prime-to-p central cyclic subgroup, by averaging for a bounded quotient.
Raise a generator to a bounded power so that its centralizer is a proper Levi, contradicting irreducibility.
acceptance: For a torus the semisimple statement does not apply: finite multiplicative subgroups have arbitrarily large cyclic quotients.

sources.locator: FKP19 Lemmas A.3, A.5, A.6, pp.62–63; LP11 Theorem 0.2, p.1106 and §12, p.1156
sources.match: The earlier paper derives the cyclic-quotient bound from the finite-subgroup theorem and root centralizers.

nodes.title: Central Γ-factors of a finite p-group
nodes.statement: For a finite p-group Σ with Γ acting by automorphisms, a central Γ-series is 1=Σ₀⊲⋯⊲Σ_n=Σ of Γ-stable normal subgroups with Σ_{i+1}/Σ_i central in Σ/Σ_i. A maximal such series has elementary abelian simple F_p[Γ]-factors, indexed 0≤i<n. Define its factor multiset up to equivariant isomorphism.
hypotheses: Finite Σ; Γ may be arbitrary.
proofSteps: Refine the ascending central series using Γ-stable subspaces.
At a maximal step both commutators and p-th powers vanish, so the factor is an elementary abelian simple module.
acceptance: Σ=1 has an empty factor multiset.

sources.locator: Appendix A before Lemma A.3, p.44
sources.match: The central factors organize the modular constituents of residual unipotent images.

nodes.statement: Any two maximal central Γ-series of a finite p-group Σ give the same multiset of simple F_p[Γ]-factors. If Σ⊂U(k) is normalized by a subgroup of P(k), all its central factors are F_p[Γ]-subquotients of Lie U, for p sufficiently large in the root datum.
hypotheses: P is parabolic with unipotent radical U and the equivariant exponential is available.
proofSteps: Apply Schreier refinement to Γ-stable central series.
Filter Σ by Σ∩U_i(k), not by replacing Σ with U(k).
The requested P-equivariant exponential identifies U_{i+1}/U_i with the corresponding Lie quotient.
acceptance: For a cyclic group of order p² with trivial Γ-action, both maximal series have exactly two trivial F_p factors.

nodes.title: Cyclotomic exclusion implies C3 and C4
nodes.statement: For p sufficiently large in G, if μ_p is not contained in F(Ad ρ̄), then M and M* have disjoint prime-field simple constituents, and C3,C4 hold. The assertion is unchanged by replacing ρ̄ with its Levi projection from a minimal residual parabolic after a finite coefficient extension.
hypotheses: G is connected split reductive; choose a minimal parabolic anew after enlarging k.
proofSteps: An isomorphism between a constituent of M and a cyclotomic twist of another would force the cyclotomic character to factor through Ad ρ̄.
Over the Levi splitting field apply the small-representation H¹ result.
Use inflation–restriction and the central factors of the residual p-kernel to rule out equivariant homomorphisms into M*.
acceptance: If μ_p⊂F then this exclusion criterion is unavailable; C3/C4 must instead be verified directly.

sources.locator: Lemma A.5 and Remark A.6, p.45
sources.match: The source criterion supplies both nonoverlap and finite-image H¹ vanishing without semisimplicity of M.

nodes.title: An abelian root subgroup faithful on the Levi center
nodes.statement: For semisimple G and parabolic P=MU at sufficiently large p, construct an abelian M-normalized subgroup A⊂U which is a product of root subgroups and whose Lie algebra a has faithful action of z(m). Choose a maximal abelian M-submodule of u and exponentiate it; its choice is not canonical.
hypotheses: The source bound depends only on the root datum; the exponential preserves the required Lie subalgebras.
proofSteps: If the kernel z₀⊂z(m) of the action were nonzero, select a nonzero z₀-weight f on u with 2f absent.
Nilpotence gives a nonzero M-submodule in u_f commuting with a.
Its self-bracket vanishes by the weight choice; adjoining it contradicts maximality.
acceptance: For the Borel in SL₂ at p odd, A=U and the toral Lie action is multiplication by 2.

sources.locator: Lemma A.7 and Remark A.8, pp.45–46

nodes.title: Corrected block criteria for GL_n
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄ take values in a parabolic of GL_n with Levi blocks r_i of dimensions n_i. Suppose p≫n, each r_i is absolutely irreducible, and r_i≄r_j⊗ψ for i≠j and ψ∈{1,κ̄,κ̄⁻¹}. Set χ_ij=(det r_i)^{n_j}(det r_j)^{−n_i}. Require jointly [F(ζ_p):F(ζ_p)∩F(χ_ij: i≠j)]>b(n). Then C2,C3,C4 hold and Levi projection injects H⁰(Γ_F,M) into z(m)∩sl_n. For a Levi-valued representation the invariants themselves lie there.
hypotheses: The determinant-field condition concerns the compositum of all character fields, not separate pairwise degrees.
proofSteps: Filter the adjoint module by block degree; its semisimplification is built from Hom(r_j,r_i), with the trace relation.
The off-diagonal invariant and twisted-invariant terms vanish by the nonisomorphism hypotheses.
Use the cyclic-quotient bound to control the adjoint splitting field through the joint determinant ratios, then apply cyclotomic exclusion.
acceptance: For three one-dimensional blocks, separate pairwise degree bounds do not imply a bound for the joint determinant field. Retain the joint-field regression in E37.

sources.match: The joint field condition and the invariant projection are the corrected forms required by the direct-sum application.

nodes.title: Classical maximal-parabolic invariant criteria
nodes.statement: Let P=MU be one of the four classical maximal parabolics of Lemma A.11 with abelian U. Assume p is sufficiently large in G, the Levi representation r_M is absolutely M-irreducible, the cyclotomic degree exceeds the root-datum constant, and im ρ̄→im r_M is not injective. Then H⁰(u)=0 implies C1. For GL block, symplectic Siegel and even orthogonal maximal-isotropic cases, H⁰(u(1))=0 implies C2; the opposite piece cannot lift to an invariant across the nontrivial U-kernel. For the orthogonal line stabilizer require also H⁰(u∨(1))=0. For GL blocks the tests are unequal dimensions or r′≄r″, respectively r′≄r″κ̄⁻¹. For GSp Siegel, u=Sym²r⊗δ⁻¹, so the tests exclude nondegenerate symmetric forms of multipliers δ and δκ̄⁻¹. For SO line stabilizer u=std⊗χ, exclude its trivial, κ̄ and κ̄⁻¹ constituents as appropriate; for SO even maximal-isotropic u=Λ²std, use the stated invariant and twisted-invariant tests.

Both exponents may be zero.

Include zero among the bounded powers; restriction and field automorphism act on the indicated sides.

nodes.title: Character separation for maximal parabolics
nodes.statement: For each maximal parabolic P of a split reductive G there are constants b,s,t,N depending only on its root datum such that, for p≫G and absolutely M-irreducible r_M, C3,C4 follow from either [F(ζ_p):F(ζ_p)∩F(χ)]>b or D(s,t,N) for χ induced by the one-dimensional adjoint-Levi quotient. All weights of the relevant adjoint constituents are bounded powers of χ after that restriction.

nodes.title: Borel-valued residual criteria
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄ take values in B(k)=T(k)U(k), U_ρ̄=im ρ̄∩U(k), and u_ρ̄ the k-span of log(U_ρ̄). Let z_{g^der}(u_ρ̄) carry the torus action via the residual torus character. Absence of 1 among its semisimple constituents gives C1; absence of κ̄⁻¹ gives C2. If for every constituent χ of g^der and σ∈Aut(k), χ^σ does not occur among constituents of g^der(1), then C3,C4 hold.
hypotheses: p≫G; use all simple prime-field subquotients, not only quotients.

Filter the Borel action to read off the stated characters.
Apply the central-factor argument and small-representation H¹ vanishing.

nodes.title: Finite-prime annihilation of the dual Sha group
nodes.statement: Under C4 there is a finite set T⊃S of trivial primes such that Sha¹_T(M*)=ker(H¹(Γ_{F,T},M*)→⊕_{v∈T}H¹(Γ_{F_v},M*)) is zero. Each successive nonzero Sha class is detected at a trivial prime outside any prescribed finite excluded set. Consequently Sha²_T(M)=0 by global duality.

proofSteps: Inflation–restriction (the pinned explicitInfRes_exact for the open normal subgroup Γ_K) and C4 inject a nonzero dual class into Hom(Γ_K,M*).
Choose a nonzero evaluation and realize it by Frobenius at a prime split in K.
Adding that prime decreases the finite-dimensional Sha¹; iterate and invoke Poitou–Tate.
acceptance: A nonzero residual dual Sha class restricts nontrivially to Γ_K under C4. Without C4 a class inflated from Gal(K/F) is invisible to primes split in K.

nodes.title: Simultaneous Sha stabilization for cyclic modules
nodes.statement: Enlarge T so that Sha¹_T(M_Z*) has minimal dimension among enlargements by trivial primes for every cyclic submodule M_Z⊂M. Also arrange the analogous minimum for Sha¹_T((M_λ)*) for every cyclic submodule M_λ⊂M*. These are dual quotients of two possibly different modules; the dual of a cyclic module need not be cyclic. There are finitely many such modules. Further enlargement by trivial primes preserves the minima.
proofSteps: Minimize one of the finitely many nonnegative dimensions at a time.
Use restriction on ramification and the local unramified condition to identify the stabilized Sha group under further enlargement.
acceptance: Use a cyclic module whose dual is not cyclic; stabilizing only cyclic submodules of the dual omits the required quotient.

nodes.title: The one-prime ramification exact sequence
nodes.statement: For T with the stabilized Sha conditions and any trivial prime w∉T, put L_{w,Z}={φ∈H¹(Γ_{F_w},M_Z):φ(τ_w)∈F_p Z}. There is an exact sequence 0→H¹(Γ_{F,T},M_Z)→H¹_{L_{w,Z}}(Γ_{F,T∪{w}},M_Z)→F_p Z→0, whose last map evaluates at τ_w. The same statement holds for the cyclic modules M_λ⊂M*. Thus every vector of F_p Z is realizable, without a remaining obstruction condition.
hypotheses: The exact local conditions are unramified away from T and unrestricted at T; all dual conditions are their annihilators.
proofSteps: Apply the Greenberg–Wiles formula to the unrestricted old local conditions and the new condition L_{w,Z}.
Stabilized dual Sha makes the dual terms cancel, so the dimension increases by one when Z≠0.
The inertia map has kernel exactly the old unramified classes, hence is surjective; for Z=0 both the increase and target are zero.
Repeat for M_λ using its separate dual-quotient stabilization.
acceptance: For Z=0 the last term is zero and no new ramification class is promised. For nonzero Z the new inertia line has F_p-dimension one, even when [k:F_p]>1.

nodes.title: Inductively chosen spanning ramification classes
nodes.statement: Under C4 choose T and marked trivial primes t₀,t_b as in Proposition 3.6. Let r=dim_Fp coker Ψ_T for localization of H¹(Γ_{F,T},M). For every c≥D_cyc+1 and finite Galois L/F containing K, unramified outside T and disjoint over K from K∞ and the fields cut out by all old classes in H¹(Γ_{F,T},M*), there are inductively chosen pairs (T_i,α_i), norm classes q_i≡1 mod p^{D_cyc} but not mod p^{D_cyc+1}, and vectors Y_i in the old local direct sum, 1≤i≤r. After each such choice an arbitrary element g_i∈Gal(L/K) may be specified; the next pair may depend on the preceding g_j. Each resulting set l_i of primes has positive upper density, lies in the Chebotarev set specifying g_i and q_i mod p^c, and admits h^{(w)}∈H¹(Γ_{F,T∪{w}},M) with old restriction Y_i and inertia values h^{(w)}(τ_w),h^{(w)}(τ_{t₀})∈F_p X_{α_i}∖{0}. The class lies in the image for M_{X_{α_i}}, and the Y_i map to an F_p-basis of coker Ψ_T.
hypotheses: The marked primes and dual basis are chosen once in the preparatory construction.
The Frobenius coset must be nonorthogonal to the chosen root vector under the calibrated pairing.
proofSteps: Choose a dual class detecting a missing cokernel direction.
Move a root direction to make its pairing nonzero, and impose the resulting nonorthogonal Frobenius coset.
Apply the one-prime sequence to M_X, and use finite pigeonhole to make old local values constant on a positive-upper-density subset.
Repeat until the F_p cokernel basis is exhausted, respecting the order of choices.
acceptance: If coker Ψ_T has F_p-dimension zero the spanning family is empty; the prescribed-vector construction can still be nonempty.

nodes.title: Ramification classes for a prescribed vector
nodes.statement: With the same preparation, every nonzero Z∈M admits a positive-upper-density set of trivial primes w and classes h_Z^{(w)} from H¹(M_Z), with h_Z^{(w)}(τ_w),h_Z^{(w)}(τ_{t₀})∈F_p Z∖{0} and constant old local restriction. The same norm and disjoint-extension Frobenius prescriptions are available; there is no assertion that this particular old restriction is a cokernel basis vector.

Use the marked prime t₀ to impose nonzero ramification in the same prime-field line.

nodes.title: Marked dual auxiliary classes

At each prime w in the prescribed families construct η_b^{(w)}=θ_b+θ_b^{(w)}∈H¹(Γ_{F,T∪{w}},M*), with inertia e_b* at both w and t_b, zero at the other t_{b′}, and unramified at t₀. Here θ_b is unramified outside T with only t_b among the marked primes, while θ_b^{(w)} is unramified at all marked primes and has inertia e_b* at w. Both restrictions to Γ_K have image in the cyclic module generated by e_b*.

Construct θ_b^{(w)} with the complementary ramification pattern and add.
Check each inertia value before passing to its cocycle field.

nodes.title: Inertia-generated extensions are disjoint
nodes.statement: Let L_i/K be finite elementary abelian p-extensions Galois over F, and let v_i be places such that all L_j with j≠i and a fixed base extension B/K are unramified at v_i. If the Γ_F-conjugates of inertia at v_i generate Gal(L_i/K), the L_i are strongly linearly disjoint over K and jointly disjoint from B, provided B is unramified at all v_i. For a product of several extensions at one place, generation must hold in the joint Galois image, not just in every projected factor.
hypotheses: The base extension B/K is finite and Galois over F. Unramified at v_i means unramified at every K-place over the chosen F-place. Finite cyclotomic layers satisfy this condition.
proofSteps: A common quotient of L_i with the compositum of the others kills its inertia at v_i.
Equivariance then kills the generated module; induct on the finite family.
For grouped extensions verify joint inertia generation explicitly before invoking the quotient argument.

nodes.title: Conditional strong disjointness from joint inertia
nodes.statement: Fix finitely many new primes w. Put L_w=∏_b K_{η_b^(w)}. For each fixed w the marked t_b inertia proves Gal(L_w/K)=∏_b M*_{e_b*}. Assume in addition that the Γ_F-conjugates of the JOINT inertia subgroup at w generate this entire product, and that a base extension B/K is unramified at every w. Then the fields L_w are strongly linearly disjoint over K and jointly disjoint from B. In particular one may take B to be any finite layer of K∞. The extra generation hypothesis is essential; FKP22 v5 Lemma 3.7 does not establish it and its unconditional all-(w,b) assertion is false under Assumption 3.1 alone.
hypotheses: The generation condition concerns the whole joint image, not every projection separately.
No unconditional mixed h/η disjointness is inferred from individual inertia generators.
proofSteps: At one fixed w use the t_b places to identify the product of the individual cyclic images.
For different w apply inertia-generated disjointness to the grouped L_w, using precisely the extra joint-generation assumption.
Pass through all finite cyclotomic layers, which are unramified away from p.
Record gap G1 for the replacement that the doubling proof actually needs under its main hypotheses; do not apply this conditional result unless its extra assumption is verified.
acceptance: Test M*=F_p(κ̄)³ with F=Q and trivial SL₂ residual representation. For two basis indices identify their cyclic lines and put ζ_w=η_1^(w)−η_2^(w). This class is unramified at w and lies in the finite group H¹(Γ_{Q,T},F_p(κ̄)).

Two distinct new primes w,w′ have ζ_w=ζ_w′. The resulting nonzero relation among four scalar cocycles persists on Γ_K, since H¹(Gal(Q(μ_p)/Q),F_p(κ̄))=0. Their four degree-p fields therefore cannot be strongly disjoint.
This example satisfies Assumption 3.1 but fails C1. It refutes the lemma in its stated scope, without refuting Theorem 5.2.

The failure is not confined to C1-failing data. Let k=F_p and suppose M* is semisimple with a simple constituent of multiplicity at least two, as for the F₄-valued residual images of FKP19 Proposition 7.8 (image A₆ or PSL₂(F₁₃), with adjoint multiplicities above one by FKP19 Remark 7.9), which satisfy C1–C4. For every k-basis the F_p[Γ_F]-span of the inertia tuple (e_b*)_b has that constituent with multiplicity at most its dimension, while ∏_b M*_{e_b*} has it with multiplicity at least the number of basis vectors meeting its isotypic part. So the inertia at w generates a proper submodule, L_w has a nontrivial subextension E_w unramified at w, and E_w lies in the finite maximal elementary abelian p-extension of K unramified outside T. Hence E_w=E_w′ for some w≠w′ and L_w∩L_w′≠K.

nodes.title: The initial lift modulo ϖ²
nodes.statement: After choosing T with Sha²_T(M)=0, a residual fixed-μ representation that has the specified local μ-lifts at every v∈T admits a global fixed-μ lift modulo ϖ². The local obstruction classes vanish by those local lifts; global duality kills the remaining Sha² obstruction. Subsequent H¹ modification can impose the specified old local congruences when the localization cokernel has been supplied by the spanning classes.
hypotheses: The added trivial places admit their chosen local lifts; killing Sha² alone does not prove local liftability.
proofSteps: Form the actual global fixed-multiplier H² obstruction using the owner’s deformation theory.
Restrict to each local μ-lift to show it lies in Sha².
Kill it, then adjust the torsor of lifts by H¹.
acceptance: A local obstruction in H² at an original ramified place is not killed by Sha²=0. Require an actual local fixed-μ lift first.

sources.locator: Paragraph after Lemma 3.7 and Proposition 3.8, p.16 (v5 has no §3.2)

nodes.title: Density selection with independent cocycle fields
nodes.statement: Suppose the finite cocycle fields used to test a Frobenius prescription are strongly disjoint over K, their degrees are bounded, and the norm prescriptions agree on the common cyclotomic subfield. If each unused independent test has conditional success proportion at least ε>0, the density of the set failing all s tests is at most (1−ε)^s. Consequently some test succeeds in any fixed positive-upper-density prime set once s is large enough.
hypotheses: The positive-upper-density set is the previously selected l_i; one cannot simply intersect an arbitrary such set with a Chebotarev set.
proofSteps: Compute finite Chebotarev densities in the product Galois group, conditional on the common field.
Bound the failure proportion by the product of the uniform failure bounds.
Choose s so that this bound is less than the upper density of l_i.
acceptance: With ε=1/2 and s independent tests, failure density is at most 2^{-s}; choose s so this is below the given upper density. No arbitrary intersection-of-positive-density assertion is used.

sources.match: The quantitative failure estimate replaces an invalid assertion about arbitrary density intersections.

nodes.title: The normalized trivial-prime local pairing
nodes.statement: Let W be a free O/ϖ^r-module with trivial local action, q_w≡1 mod ϖ^r, and W*=Hom_O(W,O/ϖ^r(1)). Choose τ_w compatibly with the chosen p-power root of unity, arithmetic σ_w, and the invariant map normalized by local reciprocity sending a uniformizer to geometric Frobenius. Then inv_w(φ∪ψ)=−⟨φ(σ_w),ψ(τ_w)⟩+⟨φ(τ_w),ψ(σ_w)⟩. In particular the two single-unramified formulas have opposite signs.
hypotheses: p is odd; the coefficients and tame-generator calibration are part of the assertion.
proofSteps: Use the local reciprocity and Kummer identifications supplied by local duality.
Evaluate an unramified character on the geometric Frobenius image of a uniformizer.
Use graded commutativity for the swapped term.
acceptance: For the unramified and tame basis u,t at a trivial prime, u∪u=t∪t=0 and u∪t=−t∪u. Reversing the Frobenius convention changes the calibrated overall sign.

nodes.title: Doubling with controlled inertia and Frobenius
nodes.statement: Given the initial mod-ϖ² lift and desired old local correction z, choose finitely many pairs of distinct trivial primes (w_i,w_i′) and h= h_old−Σ_i h^{(w_i)}+2Σ_i h^{(w_i′)}. The modification by h agrees with z at old places, has inertia −X_i at w_i and 2X_i at w_i′, and has Frobenius values in the required central torus cosets for the selected roots and norm classes. The root directions may be chosen to span M while their old local restrictions span the localization cokernel.
hypotheses: p is odd; −X_i and 2X_i must not be identified except at p=3.
The actual torus coset includes the prescribed multiplier.
proofSteps: Solve the old localization equation with the spanning classes.
Use marked dual fields and the calibrated cup pairing to translate the new-prime constraints into independent Frobenius evaluations.
Apply density selection to choose the two families.
Evaluate the explicit linear combination at each inertia generator and old place.
acceptance: For p=5 the two new inertia coefficients −1 and 2 are distinct and nonzero; demanding equal coefficients is a regression.

sources.match: The doubling formula preserves the old correction but has two different new inertia coefficients.

nodes.title: Disjointness from the higher congruence field
nodes.statement: Under C1,C3, if ρ_{n−1} is a finite-level fixed-μ lift whose image contains the full derived congruence subgroup and L=K(ρ_{n−1}(g^der)), then L is disjoint over K from the compositum of K∞ and all dual cocycle fields used in doubling. The congruence filtration of Gal(L/K) has constituents that are quotients of sums of M; its possible abelian quotients cannot occur in M*, nor in the trivial cyclotomic quotient.
hypotheses: The field is the adjoint congruence field, with the coefficient level and component splitting field fixed.
proofSteps: Use the smooth-group congruence quotients and the Lie action.
Pass a hypothetical common quotient down to a simple prime-field constituent.
Apply C3 for the dual fields and C1 for the trivial quotient, using the prime-to-p component action.
Use the module image of the whole dual compositum; this argument does not require independence among the individual dual fields.
acceptance: A common elementary abelian quotient with trivial conjugation is excluded by C1; one with dual constituents is excluded by C3. Neither follows from pairwise field intersections alone.

sources.match: This allows new auxiliary primes to satisfy higher-level Frobenius constraints.

nodes.title: Controlled compatible finite-level lifts
nodes.statement: Assume C1,C3,C4 and specified local μ-lifts λ_v for v∈S. For every prescribed finite accuracy and avoidance set there are increasing finite ramification sets T_n and compatible fixed-μ lifts ρ_n:Γ_{F,T_n}→G(O/ϖ^n), n≥2, with ρ_n|Γ_{F_v} strictly conjugate to λ_v modulo ϖ^n at every original v∈S, and full derived congruence image at every level n. At an early auxiliary place the tower follows a fixed smooth O-valued local lift. At a late auxiliary place of norm depth D_cyc and ramification index e=v_ϖ(p), it has the root-type form: ρ_{eD_cyc} is central, α(ρ(σ))=q, and every root β has β(ρ_{eD_cyc+1}(σ))≠1 at its first noncentral level. New primes can be required to avoid any fixed finite set.
hypotheses: The initial finite accuracy is chosen deep enough for relative theory. The early/late cutoff eD_cyc is fixed by the coefficient ramification index and the roots of unity in K; it is not a free depth parameter.
The tower alone makes no assertion of one finite ramification set in its inverse limit.
proofSteps: Initialize by doubling, choosing root directions spanning M.
At each step use congruence-field disjointness to impose the next finite-level Frobenius values.
Choose a maximal torus in general position with respect to the required hyperplanes and use the smooth root lifting functor.
Apply doubling to remove the old local error, then keep the lifts compatible while enlarging T_n.
acceptance: For e=2,D_cyc=1 the fixed first noncentral level is 3. Increasing the relative depth M does not change that cutoff.

sources.match: The controlled tower supplies the deep starting representation for relative Selmer annihilation.

nodes.title: Relative Selmer images
nodes.statement: For compatible local conditions L_{r,v}⊂H¹(Γ_{F_v},M_r), 1≤r≤n, define RelSel_r=im(H¹_{L_r}(Γ_{F,S},M_r)→H¹_{L_1}(Γ_{F,S},M_1)) and RelDual_r by the analogous reduction for M_r*=Hom_O(M_r,O/ϖ^r(1)) with annihilator local conditions. These are k-subspaces of the residual Selmer groups. Balanced means equality of the cardinalities of the full primal and dual Selmer groups at every level 1≤r≤n, not an assumed equality of their images.
hypotheses: M_r is the actual adjoint module of a fixed finite lift, with coefficient reductions; the local conditions are compatible with them.
proofSteps: Use the existing Selmer kernel and coefficient functoriality.
Take its linear image under reduction.
Use local duality for the annihilator conditions, without identifying the full residual Selmer group with the reduction image.
acceptance: The image of the identity on any Selmer space is that space, agreeing with Submodule.map id.

sources.match: The image, rather than the full residual group, is the object killed by relative deformation theory.

api.name: Lifting.relative_selmer_image.image_iff
api.statement: A residual Selmer class belongs to RelSel_r iff it has a level-r Selmer preimage.

api.name: Lifting.relative_selmer_image.level_one
api.statement: RelSel_1 is the full residual Selmer group, since reduction at level one is the identity.

api.name: Lifting.relative_selmer_image.decreasing
api.statement: For r≤s, RelSel_s⊂RelSel_r, and likewise for the dual, whenever the indicated reductions preserve local conditions.

tests.name: Lifting.relative_selmer_image.identity
tests.statement: The image of the identity on any Selmer space is that space, agreeing with Submodule.map id.

tests.name: Lifting.relative_selmer_image.zero_reduction
tests.statement: For a nonzero source annihilated by the chosen reduction map, its relative image is zero even if the residual target is nonzero.

tests.name: Lifting.relative_selmer_image.strict_image
tests.statement: The image of k→k², a↦(a,0), is one-dimensional and is not all the residual target.

uses.how: Only classes with nonzero relative reduction need a detection prime.
Kills both relative images while allowing full level-M Selmer groups to remain nonzero.

nodes.title: Exactness for compatible local cocycle lattices
nodes.statement: Suppose the preimages Z_{r,v} of L_{r,v} contain B¹ and fit into 0→Z_{a,v}→Z_{a+b,v}→Z_{b,v}→0 for all a,b>0 with a+b≤n. Then H¹_{L_a}(M_a)→H¹_{L_{a+b}}(M_{a+b})→H¹_{L_b}(M_b) is exact in the middle, and the first map is injective if H⁰(Γ_F,M_1)=0. The annihilator conditions give 0→Z^⊥_{b,v}→Z^⊥_{a+b,v}→Z^⊥_{a,v}, exact without a final surjectivity assertion, and the corresponding dual Selmer sequence with a,b reversed. The first map in the dual Selmer sequence is injective only under H⁰(Γ_F,M_1*)=0; middle exactness does not require either reduction map to be surjective.
proofSteps: Lift representatives in the cocycle diagram and use the local short exact sequences.
Use absence of residual invariants for uniqueness of the global preimage.
Dualize the coefficient maps using local Tate pairings; reverse their order.
acceptance: A coefficient reduction can have a nonzero connecting obstruction. Only middle exactness is asserted; final surjectivity is not automatic.

sources.match: The proof provides middle exactness, not automatic surjectivity of a Selmer reduction.

nodes.title: Balanced local conditions give balanced relative images
nodes.statement: Under C1,C2 and the cocycle exactness hypotheses, equality |Sel_r|=|DualSel_r| for every 1≤r≤n implies dim_k RelSel_n=dim_k RelDual_n. The local numerical conditions |L_{r,v}|=|H⁰_v(M_r)| away from p and |L_{r,v}|=|H⁰_v(M_r)|·|O/ϖ^r|^{[F_v:Q_p]dim Flag(G⁰)} at p, together with oddness and total reality in characteristic zero, supply the full-level balance by Greenberg–Wiles. In positive characteristic there is no p-adic or archimedean correction.
proofSteps: Apply the coefficient exactness theorem at (n−1,1).
Compute image cardinalities by dividing adjacent full Selmer cardinalities.
Use the owner’s global cardinality formula and the stated local cardinalities to obtain equality at all levels.
acceptance: If full level-r Selmer groups have equal orders at r=n,n−1, the orders of their residual images agree after dividing by the corresponding kernels.

sources.locator: FKP19 Lemma 6.3, p.45; FKP22 proof of Theorem 5.2, pp.24–25
sources.match: Equality at finite levels yields equality for their mod-p images.

nodes.title: Uniform torsion in compact Lie-group cohomology
nodes.statement: Let Γ be a compact p-adic analytic group with semisimple Lie algebra and let V be a finite free O-module with continuous O-linear Γ-action. If V⊗Q_p has no Lie(Γ)-invariants, then for every i≥0 a single power of ϖ, depending on i,Γ,V and independent of r, kills H^i(Γ,V/ϖ^r). For i=1 the uniform bound holds without the no-invariants condition, using Whitehead in degrees 1 and 2. These are the continuous cohomology groups for the actual action, including its finite component action.
hypotheses: Use a sufficiently small open analytic subgroup and transfer across its finite index; a reductive Lie algebra with nonzero center does not meet the stated semisimple hypothesis.
proofSteps: Choose an open normal p-valued subgroup of finite index (requested from LocallyAnalyticDistributionsPartII ND.0; for open subgroups of G(O) the deep congruence subgroups of upstream RG2.0.3).

On it, use the finite free resolution over the completed group ring and the Ext description of continuous cohomology (requested from NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa NE.0) to get finite generation of H^i(Γ,V) and a bounded complex computing all H^i(Γ,V/ϖ^r).

Identify rational cohomology with Lie-algebra cohomology on that subgroup (Lazard V (2.4.10), requested from NE.0) and apply semisimple Lie-algebra vanishing, with only Whitehead H¹,H² in the degree-one statement (requested from AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.1a).
Finite generation and the universal-coefficient sequence of the bounded complex make the torsion exponent independent of r; pass to Γ through finite-index invariants (Hochschild–Serre).
acceptance: For Γ with Lie algebra sl₂ the Whitehead H¹,H² input yields the degree-one bound even for a trivial rank-one lattice. A Lie algebra with central Q_p factor does not satisfy this semisimple hypothesis.

sources.locator: FKP19 Lemma B.1 and proof, p.64; Lazard V, Theorems 2.2.2.3, 2.2.3.1 and 2.4.10, pp.165–166,178–179
sources.match: The analytic comparison is an explicit prerequisite of the uniform finite-coefficient bound.

sources.locator: III Proposition 3.1.3, pp.91–92; III Theorem 3.1.7.4, p.94; V §§2.2.2–2.2.3, pp.165–166 and Theorem 2.4.10, pp.178–179
sources.match: Small analytic groups admit the finite completed-group-algebra resolution and rational cohomology comparison; pass to the full group through finite-index invariants.

nodes.title: Vanishing of sufficiently deep H¹ reduction
nodes.statement: For Γ,V as in the compact Lie bound, assume H⁰(Γ,V/ϖ)=0. For every m≥1 there is N such that for every N′≥N the coefficient reduction H¹(Γ,V/ϖ^{N′})→H¹(Γ,V/ϖ^m) is zero. In the adjoint application use the inverse image in the p-adic adjoint group of the full Γ_F image, including component action; C1 supplies its residual invariant vanishing.
proofSteps: Use the coefficient exact sequence and H⁰ vanishing to identify the transition image with a high power of ϖ times an H¹ group.
Apply the uniform torsion exponent.
Apply the bound to the full compact group, not only to its connected component preimage.
acceptance: The reduction map to level m is zero for every larger level beyond N, not merely along one subsequence.

sources.locator: FKP19 Corollary B.2 and proof, p.64; FKP22 §5, pp.23–24
sources.match: The full Galois image is necessary when disconnected components remove adjoint invariants.

nodes.title: The relative auxiliary-prime set Q_N
nodes.statement: Fix e|M,N with N≥4M, a fixed-μ lift ρ_N whose image contains the full derived congruence kernel, and F_N=F(ρ̄,Adρ_N), F_N*=F_N(μ_{p^{N/e}}). Q_N consists of trivial primes w unramified for ρ_N with q_w≡1 mod ϖ^M and q_w≢1 mod ϖ^{M+1}, ρ_M|Γ_{F_w} central, and a split maximal torus T and root α such that ρ_N(σ_w)∈T, α(ρ_N(σ_w))=q_w, and β(ρ_{M+1}(σ_w))≠1 for every root β. A member includes the chosen (T,α).
hypotheses: M and N are positive multiples of e, N≥4M and M>eD_cyc; choose M large enough for deep reduction vanishing.
Central at level M is not a requirement of triviality in the full group.
proofSteps: Express all conditions in the finite Galois group of F_N*/F.
Use full congruence image and disjointness from the cyclotomic extension to show this is a nonempty Chebotarev condition.
acceptance: A trivial prime with q_w≡1 mod ϖ^{M+1} fails membership.

sources.match: The first noncentral level must avoid every root hyperplane.

api.name: Lifting.auxiliary_prime_set.central_reduction
api.statement: A Q_N prime has central ρ_M and trivial action on M_r for r≤M.

api.name: Lifting.auxiliary_prime_set.root_norm
api.statement: Its chosen α satisfies α(ρ_N(σ_w))=q_w, with exact norm depth M.

api.name: Lifting.auxiliary_prime_set.positive_density
api.statement: The compatible finite Frobenius condition is nonempty and has positive Chebotarev density.

tests.name: Lifting.auxiliary_prime_set.wrong_depth
tests.statement: A trivial prime with q_w≡1 mod ϖ^{M+1} fails membership.

tests.name: Lifting.auxiliary_prime_set.other_root
tests.statement: Satisfying the α equation while some other β is 1 at level M+1 fails membership.

tests.name: Lifting.auxiliary_prime_set.adjoint
tests.statement: For adjoint G, central reduction is the identity; for GL_n a scalar need not be the identity.

uses.how: Gives the stable root lifting fibers and rank-one unramified quotients.
Specifies the primes at which both relative classes are detected.

nodes.title: Relative root local conditions
nodes.statement: At w∈Q_N let Z^α_{r,w} be the local cocycle lattice of FKP19 Lemma 3.5 for the chosen ρ_N,T,α and let L^α_{r,w} be its image in H¹(M_r), 1≤r≤M. It contains coboundaries and is generated by divided coboundaries, unramified toral directions in ker(dα), and the ramified root direction g_α. Its dual condition is its local Tate annihilator. The root lifting functor is supplied by the local deformation owner; this definition selects its relative cohomological condition.
hypotheses: N≥4M; use the actual lattice, not merely its dimension or a formal-smoothness assertion.
proofSteps: Import the root lifting functor and its explicit cocycle lattice from the local owner.
Take its H¹ image and the local annihilator.
Use the generator formula to prove coefficient exactness and cardinalities.
acceptance: The primal unramified quotient is generated by the σ_w value dα∨(1).

sources.match: The lattice controls finite lifting fibers even when the local residual representation is trivial.

api.name: Lifting.root_local_condition.coefficient_exact
api.statement: For a+b≤M the lattices fit into 0→Z^α_a→Z^α_{a+b}→Z^α_b→0.

api.name: Lifting.root_local_condition.fiber_stability
api.statement: For m≥N−M and r≤M the nonempty fibers of the relative root lifting functor from level m+r to m are stable under Z^α_r.

api.name: Lifting.root_local_condition.balanced_cardinality
api.statement: |L^α_r|=|H⁰_w(M_r)| and each primal or dual unramified quotient by its intersection with L^α_r or its annihilator is O/ϖ^r.

tests.name: Lifting.root_local_condition.coroot
tests.statement: The primal unramified quotient is generated by the σ_w value dα∨(1).

tests.name: Lifting.root_local_condition.dual_root
tests.statement: The dual quotient is detected by evaluation on g_α and has length r, not one independent of r.

tests.name: Lifting.root_local_condition.missing_generator
tests.statement: The unramified ker(dα) directions alone omit the ramified root class and fail the balanced-cardinality and fiber-stability contracts.

uses.how: Coefficient exactness and cardinality make relative Selmer balance possible.
The two rank-one quotients allow primal/dual detection at one prime.

nodes.title: Cocycle conditions near smooth local points
nodes.statement: At each prescribed O-valued local lift lying at a smooth point of the generic local deformation space, there are an analytic neighborhood Y and sufficiently deep integral reductions such that, for every bounded r, the nonempty fibers from level m+r to m in Y are stable under submodules Z_{r,v} containing B¹ and satisfying coefficient short exactness. Away from p their H¹ images have size |H⁰_v(M_r)|; at p on a Hodge–Tate regular de Rham component their size is |H⁰_v(M_r)|·|O/ϖ^r|^{[F_v:Q_p]dim Flag(G⁰)}. One finite coefficient extension provides smooth points in each chosen component arbitrarily close to the specified point, with approximation depth measured by the original ϖ.
hypotheses: Use the local generic-fiber and potentially semistable-ring suppliers; this does not assert formal smoothness of the entire integral local ring.
proofSteps: Apply the local smooth-point analytic-neighborhood theorem and choose an integral tangent lattice.
Use its divided coboundaries and tangent basis to identify the cocycle lattice and lifting action.
Use the local generic dimension formula to obtain the cardinality.
Apply the coefficient-extension approximation lemma before choosing the global approximation depth.
acceptance: For a smooth fixed-determinant GL₂ point away from p the quotient tangent condition has cardinality |H⁰_v(sl₂_r)|. At a p-adic place multiply by |O/ϖ^r|^{[F_v:Q_p]}.

sources.locator: FKP19 Proposition 4.7 and Lemma 4.9, pp.22–25; FKP22 proof of Theorem 5.2, pp.24–25
sources.match: These local conditions preserve the chosen characteristic-zero components while the global tower changes.

nodes.title: Cohomology on the finite splitting field
nodes.statement: Under C1–C4 and the deep choice of M, for the controlled lift ρ_N with N≥4M the map H¹(Gal(F_N*/F),M_M)→H¹(Gal(F_N*/F),M_1) is zero, and H¹(Gal(F_N*/F),M_M*)=0. In particular any level-M primal class with nonzero residual reduction, and any nonzero residual reduction of a dual class, restrict nontrivially to Γ_{F_N*}.
proofSteps: Apply inflation–restriction through F_N and the cyclotomic extension; abelian conjugation and C1 kill the extra primal homomorphisms.
Use deep Lie cohomology reduction vanishing for the adjoint group with full component action.
For the dual use C4 and the fact that the maximal elementary abelian quotient of the congruence-plus-cyclotomic kernel is a quotient of M⊕F_p.
C3 and C2 kill its equivariant maps to M*.
acceptance: For a primal finite-image class, only its mod-ϖ image is forced to vanish. Replacing this conclusion by H¹ at level M being zero is too strong.

sources.match: The primal conclusion is reduction vanishing, whereas the dual conclusion is actual finite-level H¹ vanishing.

nodes.title: A simultaneous root-position lemma
nodes.statement: For a split simple group H over finite k and sufficiently large p depending only on its root datum, any nonzero A∈Lie(H) and B∈Lie(H)* admit a split maximal torus T and root α such that A∉ker(dα|t)⊕⊕_β g_β and B does not annihilate g_α. The corresponding finite-ring assertion holds for nonzero A at its first nonzero ϖ-adic layer and residual nonzero B. For H of type A₁ the bound is p≥3.
hypotheses: The adjoint Lie algebra is simple and the invariant pairing is perfect under the standing prime bound.
proofSteps: Each failure condition is a proper closed subset of the group acting on a fixed root pair.
In the big Bruhat cell clear torus denominators to bound the polynomial degrees uniformly in A,B.
Count zeros over finite k to find a point outside the two failure loci.
Lift through the smooth group and use the congruence Lie action to pass through higher coefficient levels.
For sl₂ check the three failure cases by explicit unipotent and Weyl conjugations.
acceptance: In sl₂ take A=diag(1,−1) and B evaluating the upper-right entry: the standard torus and upper root satisfy both tests for p odd.

sources.locator: FKP19 Proposition 6.8 and proof, pp.47–49; FKP22 proof of Corollary 5.5, pp.26–27
sources.match: The finite-field counting argument is the key Lie-theoretic prerequisite for simultaneous detection.

nodes.title: One prime detects both relative classes
nodes.statement: Suppose g^der consists of one π₀(G)-orbit of simple factors. For any finite Q⊂Q_N and level-M Selmer classes φ,ψ with nonzero relative reductions, there is w∈Q_N∖Q such that φ|Γ_{F_w}∉L^α_{M,w} and ψ̄|Γ_{F_w}∉(L^α_{1,w})^⊥ for its chosen (T,α). The prime may avoid any prescribed finite set.
hypotheses: Choose one simple factor on which both restricted class images have nonzero projection; transitivity supplies it.
No linear-disjointness assumption on the primal and dual cocycle fields is made.
proofSteps: Use finite-image vanishing to restrict nontrivially to Γ_{F_N*}.
Choose γ₂ outside the union of the kernels of the two projections to the same simple factor.
Apply simultaneous root position to φ(γ₂) and ψ̄(γ₂).
Choose γ₁ with the Q_N Frobenius condition by congruence/cyclotomic disjointness.
Among γ₂^rγ₁ for r=0,1,2 at most two choices fail the two required evaluations; Chebotarev realizes a successful one.
acceptance: If g=g₁⊕g₂ and φ(γ) lies only in g₁ while ψ(γ) lies only in g₂*, this single γ is unsuitable; choose outside both projection kernels before selecting a root.

sources.match: The same-factor choice repairs the projection step without reintroducing the earlier linear-disjointness hypothesis.

nodes.title: Finite-prime annihilation of relative Selmer images
nodes.statement: For balanced compatible local conditions at the finite starting set S′, and one π₀(G)-orbit of simple factors, there is a finite Q⊂Q_N such that both level-M relative Selmer and relative dual Selmer images for S′∪Q vanish, using the root local condition at every w∈Q. While either relative image is nonzero one can add a detection prime that strictly decreases the cardinality of the full level-M Selmer group. The number of primes is not bounded merely by the initial relative dimension.
proofSteps: Use relative balance to select a primal and a dual class with nonzero reductions.
At a detection prime enlarge the root condition temporarily by the unramified condition; its quotient is O/ϖ^M.
The detected dual class generates the full rank-one quotient; two local-condition comparisons show the enlarged global Selmer group equals the old one.
The detected primal class fails the root condition, so imposing it strictly decreases the finite full-level cardinality.
Iterate; balance then kills both relative images.
acceptance: A relative residual image can remain the same for one step while the full level-M order decreases. The termination measure is the positive integer full order.

sources.locator: FKP19 Theorem 6.9 and Remark 6.10, pp.49–50; FKP22 proof of Theorem 5.2, pp.24–25
sources.match: The induction decreases full finite-level cardinality rather than asserting a one-step relative-dimension drop.

nodes.title: Reduction to adjoint factor orbits
nodes.statement: The fixed-multiplier lifting problem reduces, through G/Z⁰_{G⁰}, to its π₀(G)-orbits of simple adjoint factors. Solve each orbit problem with its common finite component quotient and recombine by the corresponding fiber product. The prime-to-p central isogeny and the fixed multiplier recover a lift to the original G, preserving local conjugacy/components and full derived congruence image.
hypotheses: The component quotient is common to the orbit representations; their products are not unrestricted direct products.
proofSteps: Decompose the connected adjoint root datum into component orbits.
Apply the one-orbit theorem to each finite quotient problem, allowing a common finite ramification set and coefficient extension.
Use the fiber-product description to recombine.
Use the prime-to-p isogeny on congruence kernels and the fixed quotient to lift back.
acceptance: For two simple factors exchanged by π₀(G), one must work with their orbit and common component quotient. Independent direct products would lose that quotient.

sources.locator: FKP19 Claim 6.13, pp.51–52; FKP22 proof of Theorem 5.2, p.24
sources.match: The reduction accounts for disconnected groups and the central lifting datum.

nodes.title: Compatible lifts over one finite ramification set
nodes.statement: After level-M relative dual Selmer vanishing, the controlled lift can be extended to compatible fixed-μ lifts τ_n:Γ_{F,S′∪Q}→G(O/ϖ^n) for all n, preserving the selected local neighborhoods and root conditions. In the induction retain an auxiliary lift ρ_{n+M} reducing to τ_n; choose τ_{n+1} from its next reduction, then modify the deeper auxiliary lift. The deeper lifts need not themselves remain compatible beyond the retained level. Their inverse limit is continuous, unramified outside the same finite S′∪Q, and lies on the prescribed local components.
proofSteps: Lift the finite global representation with the local conditions, identifying the obstruction by Poitou–Tate.
Use the vanishing relative dual image to solve the local discrepancy at the next retained level.
Modify by a primal level-M cohomology class while preserving the chosen local lifting fibers.
Induct with a moving M-level buffer and take the inverse limit of the τ_n.
acceptance: At one induction step retain τ_n and a lift to n+M. After alteration only agreement with the retained level is imposed on the buffer; demanding full compatibility of buffers is unnecessary.

sources.locator: FKP19 Claim 6.14 and proof, pp.53–55; FKP22 proof of Theorem 5.2, pp.24–25
sources.match: Compatibility is imposed on the retained τ_n, not on every deeper auxiliary lift.

nodes.title: Finite detection of full congruence image
nodes.statement: There is N₁ depending on G and O such that any closed subgroup P⊂Ĝ^der(O) surjecting onto Ĝ^der(O/ϖ^{N₁}) equals Ĝ^der(O). The assertion holds after the fixed finite coefficient extension with its own N₁. Consequently the finite initial image condition in the compatible lifting construction ensures full derived congruence image in its limit.
proofSteps: The congruence kernel is a topologically finitely generated pro-p group.
Its Frattini subgroup is open, hence contains a sufficiently deep congruence kernel.
Surjectivity at that depth gives surjectivity on the Frattini quotient and therefore topological generation.
Use closedness to identify the subgroup with the full kernel.
acceptance: A closed proper subgroup cannot surject onto the Frattini quotient. Omitting closedness admits a proper dense subgroup of a finitely generated pro-p group.

sources.match: The fixed finite congruence test replaces indefinitely many new image-generating primes.

nodes.title: Geometric lifting with prescribed components
nodes.statement: Let the lifting datum satisfy C1–C4, with p sufficiently large depending only on G. If F is a number field assume F totally real and ρ̄ odd. For each v∈S fix a local μ-lift λ_v, de Rham with regular Hodge–Tate cocharacters when v|p, and an irreducible characteristic-zero local component containing it (of its fixed Hodge/inertial type at p). There is a finite extension O′/O depending only on these local lifts and components such that for every t≥1 and every finite avoidance set S₀ disjoint from S there are a finite S̃⊃S with S̃∩S₀=∅ and a continuous fixed-μ lift ρ:Γ_{F,S̃}→G(O′), whose image contains Ĝ^der(O′). For all v∈S it lies on the chosen component and is congruent modulo the original ϖ^t to a Ĝ(O′)-conjugate of λ_v. In characteristic zero it is geometric; in positive characteristic it is finitely ramified. In particular its Zariski closure contains G^der.
hypotheses: O′ is chosen before t; S̃ and ρ can depend on t.
Full derived image does not imply density in the central multiplier torus.
proofSteps: Approximate the local points by smooth points using one coefficient extension.
Construct a sufficiently deep controlled tower segment and balanced cocycle conditions.
Reduce to adjoint factor orbits, annihilate relative Selmer, and complete over a finite ramification set.
Retain a level above N₁ to force the full congruence image.
Track local neighborhoods, coefficient extension, avoidance, and component membership throughout.
acceptance: For a torus the derived-image conclusion is vacuous, but the chosen multiplier still determines the lift. For GL₂ it is fixed determinant and full principal SL₂-congruence image.

sources.locator: Theorem 5.2 (Theorem E) and proof, pp.23–25; footnotes 6–7, pp.23–24 (v5 has no Remark 5.7)
sources.match: This is the main target; the coefficient field can be fixed independently of the requested approximation depth.

nodes.title: The sl₂ small-prime refinement
nodes.statement: If g^der=sl₂, the main geometric lifting theorem holds for every p≥3 under the same C1–C4, local-lift and oddness assumptions. No assertion that those residual hypotheses follow automatically from p≥3 is included.
proofSteps: Root vectors span sl₂ for p odd.
The required torus regularity is the nonvanishing of the single root differential.
Use the explicit sl₂ simultaneous-root-position argument.
All other large-prime uses in the proof were only for obtaining the residual hypotheses, which are now assumed directly.
acceptance: At p=3 all factors 2 and −1 in the doubling argument remain nonzero. The SL₂ root-position calculation has no larger-prime counting assumption.

sources.match: The proof isolates the exact places where the large-prime hypothesis is needed.

nodes.title: Finitely ramified lifts without oddness
nodes.statement: For any number field F and a lifting datum satisfying C1–C4, replace oddness and the p-adic regular de Rham hypothesis by local μ-lifts at v|p that are smooth points on generic framed components of dimension (1+[F_v:Q_p])dim(G^der). Keep the other local hypotheses. For every t there are a finite coefficient extension and finite ramification set and a fixed-μ lift with full derived congruence image, approximating the specified local lifts modulo ϖ^t up to strict conjugacy. The conclusion does not assert geometricity.
proofSteps: Use the unrestricted smooth local component dimensions in the cardinality calculation.
Replace equality of Selmer cardinalities by the inequality required for the same annihilation argument, accounting for the actual infinite places.
Carry out the finite-ramification construction and full-image argument.
acceptance: At a real place p odd makes all positive-degree cohomology vanish on the order-two decomposition group. Unrestricted local conditions give the required inequality without oddness.

sources.match: The larger local tangent spaces replace the oddness-based balance.

nodes.title: Recovery of the irreducible lifting theorem
nodes.statement: For F totally real, an odd residual representation whose restriction to Γ_{F̃(ζ_p)} is absolutely G⁰-irreducible, with [F̃(ζ_p):F̃]>a_G and the prescribed regular local μ-lifts, satisfies the residual hypotheses of the main theorem for p≫G. It therefore has the finitely ramified geometric lift and local approximation of FKP19 Theorem 6.11. Here F̃ is the component splitting field, not the full residual field.
hypotheses: This specialization inherits gap G1 through the main geometric lifting theorem: the failure of FKP22 Lemma 3.7 also occurs for some absolutely irreducible residual images (see E45). FKP19 Theorem 6.11 has its own proof, through the field K′ of FKP19 Definition 5.8, p.29, which avoids Lemma 3.7; that route is not planned in this roadmap.
proofSteps: Apply the absolutely irreducible finite-image and bounded cyclic quotient inputs to verify C1–C4.
Use inflation–restriction across the prime-to-p component extension.
Apply the main geometric theorem and retain its coefficient/component control.
acceptance: Absolute G-irreducibility on Γ_{F(ζ_p)} is retained explicitly. Irreducibility merely on Γ_F is not a substitute.

sources.locator: FKP19 Theorem 6.11 and Corollary A.7, pp.50–51,63–64; FKP22 §1.2, pp.5–6
sources.match: The new theorem contains the earlier irreducible result as a verified specialization.

nodes.title: Changing the residual lattice to a Levi projection
nodes.statement: Let G be connected reductive and ρ:Γ→G(O) continuous with residual image in a parabolic P=MU. After a finite totally ramified coefficient extension O′/O there is g∈G(Frac O′) such that gρg⁻¹ is O′-valued and its reduction is the Levi projection of ρ̄. If P is minimal containing the residual image this reduction is its G-semisimplification. Conjugation preserves the characteristic-zero Zariski closure up to conjugacy, but need not preserve the full integral congruence kernel.
proofSteps: Choose a cocharacter with zero weights on M and positive weights on U.
Multiply it so it lifts through the relevant central isogeny to an actual cocharacter of G.
Choose the ramification index large enough that conjugation by its value on the new uniformizer keeps all negative-root coordinates integral and makes the positive-root coordinates vanish residually.
Apply the existing minimal-parabolic semisimplification theorem.
acceptance: For SL₂ the adjoint cocharacter diag(t,1) need not lift to SL₂ without a square root; multiply the cocharacter or make the specified coefficient extension.

sources.match: The ramification and cocharacter scaling are necessary to obtain an integral conjugate with the specified reduction.

nodes.title: Arbitrarily large controlled extension spaces
nodes.statement: Let W≠0 and W′ be finite F_p[Γ_{F,S}]-modules and let 0≠W⁰⊂W be an F_p-subspace. For every integer d there is a finite set T outside S, trivial for both W and W′ and with q_v≡1 mod p, such that dim_Fp H¹_L(Γ_{F,S∪T},W)>d, where L_v=0 at old places and at new places inertia takes values in W⁰. The new sets may avoid any fixed finite set.
proofSteps: Choose completely split primes for both coefficient actions and μ_p.
At each new prime the allowed local space exceeds the unramified space by dim W⁰.
Apply Greenberg–Wiles and the local-condition comparison formula to obtain an unbounded lower bound.
acceptance: For W=F_p(χ) and any j the construction gives j independent classes after a controlled finite enlargement of T; it does not claim an infinite-dimensional group for one fixed T.

sources.match: Triviality for W itself is required for the local Hom description.

nodes.title: Parabolic representations with full abelian radical image
nodes.statement: For connected G, P=MU, a Levi-valued residual ρ̄ and an abelian M-normalized product A⊂U of root subgroups, there are finitely many ρ̄-trivial new primes T and ρ̄′:Γ_{F,S∪T}→A⋊M with projection ρ̄, image containing A(k), and local restrictions conjugate to ρ̄ at every old place. At each new place the image lies in A(k) and inertia in a single chosen root subgroup.
proofSteps: Use the split semidirect product to identify lifts of ρ̄ with continuous cocycles in A(k).
For every prime-field line in each selected root coordinate use the controlled extension-space theorem to obtain a nontrivially ramified class supported at disjoint new primes.
Sum these classes; local inertia supplies generators for all A(k), while zero old local classes give conjugacy there.
acceptance: For an abelian radical A with two F_p directions, use enough independent classes to make the joint image all of A; separate nonzero projections alone would not suffice.

sources.match: The full A(k) image permits invariant removal while preserving old local data.

nodes.title: Local lifts of abelian-unipotent residual image
nodes.statement: Let q_v≡1 mod p, p odd, and let the local residual image lie in an abelian root subgroup A(k), with inertia in U_α(k). It has an O-valued lift after coefficient extension: choose lifts u₁∈A(O),u₂∈U_α(O), put t=α∨(√q_v) with √q_v≡1 mod ϖ, and send σ_v to tu₁ and τ_v to u₂. If a fixed multiplier μ is required, multiply the Frobenius value by a central lift of μ(σ_v) and verify that μ is unramified and residually trivial here.
hypotheses: The central multiplier lift uses the prime-to-p central isogeny; the uncorrected formula only has trivial multiplier.
proofSteps: Use Hensel for the specified square root.
The coroot acts on its root group with weight 2 and A is abelian, giving the tame relation.
The central correction changes the quotient without changing the tame conjugation relation.
acceptance: If μ(σ_w) is a nonidentity pro-p central value, a trivial-multiplier lift fails the local datum. Correct it through the prime-to-p central isogeny.

sources.match: The formula gives explicit local liftability at the newly introduced primes; fixed multiplier needs the central adjustment.

nodes.title: Removing adjoint invariants by an extension
nodes.statement: Assume H⁰(Γ_F,M)=z(m)∩g^der for Levi-valued ρ̄ and the local regular μ-lifts. Choose A as in the faithful-center root subgroup theorem. The parabolic extension ρ̄′ can be chosen with H⁰(Γ_F,Adρ̄′ g^der)=0 and with all required local μ-lifts. If H⁰(Γ_F,M*)=0 then also H⁰(Γ_F,(Adρ̄′ g^der)*)=0. For the latter comparison use the joint images of (ρ̄′,κ̄) and (ρ̄,κ̄), which have the same prime-to-p quotient; invariance vanishing does not follow merely from equality of semisimplifications.
proofSteps: The new image contains A(k) and, by the semidirect-product splitting, the original Levi image.
Old invariants therefore lie in the Levi center, and faithfulness of its action on a kills them.
For the twisted module compare the joint cyclotomic images and their p-kernels.
Use the explicit unipotent local lift at new primes and the unchanged old local classes.
acceptance: Adding a semisimple-equivalent extension need not preserve H⁰. Check actual image containment of A(k) after adjoining μ_p before applying the invariant computation.

sources.locator: Lemma 6.5 and proof of Corollary 6.6, p.30
sources.match: The joint-image argument supplies the valid twisted-invariant comparison.

nodes.title: Geometric lifts of Levi-valued residual representations
nodes.statement: Let G be connected, F totally real, and ρ̄ odd with image in a Levi M of P. Assume p≫G, regular geometric local μ-lifts, H⁰(Γ_F,M_ad)=z(m)∩g^der and H⁰(Γ_F,M_ad*)=0. Suppose either μ_p⊄F(Adρ̄), or P is maximal, ρ̄ is absolutely M-irreducible and satisfies the D alternative of maximal separation. Then after finite coefficient extension there is a finitely ramified geometric fixed-μ lift of the original ρ̄ whose Zariski closure contains G^der. The conclusion is derived Zariski density, not necessarily full integral congruence image after changing its residual lattice.
proofSteps: Create the full abelian-root extension and remove invariants.
Use cyclotomic exclusion or maximal separation to verify C3,C4 for the extension.
Apply the main lifting theorem to that extension.
Change the integral lattice to recover the original Levi-valued residual representation; characteristic-zero derived density survives.
acceptance: An even GL₂ diagonal residual representation over Q is outside the geometric conclusion. At real places the added p-primary extension is conjugate to its Levi projection.

sources.match: Oddness and the absolute-Levi-irreducibility requirement in the second alternative are retained.

nodes.title: The corrected torus criterion
nodes.statement: For ρ̄ valued in a split maximal torus T, the equality H⁰(Γ_F,M)=t∩g^der holds precisely when every root character α∘ρ̄ is nontrivial. The dual invariant condition additionally excludes κ̄⁻¹ from the toral and root constituents. Together with the Borel separation criterion, oddness and the required local lifts, these hypotheses imply the Levi geometric lifting theorem. Merely requiring that the image lie in no proper subtorus is insufficient.
proofSteps: Decompose g^der into t^der and its root lines.
Read the two invariant conditions from the actual characters.
Apply the Borel criterion and the Levi theorem.
acceptance: For SL₂ and a nontrivial quadratic χ, diag(χ,χ⁻¹) has trivial root character; its invariant Lie algebra is sl₂, so the purported generic torus case must be excluded.

sources.match: Rootwise nontriviality is the correct test for torus invariants.

nodes.title: A corrected GSp₄ Siegel example
nodes.statement: Let r be the absolutely irreducible residual representation of a classical newform of weight a≥2, and δ an odd finite residual character. For the GSp₄ Siegel Levi (r,δ), require the invariant and dual-invariant exclusions on both Sym²r⊗δ⁻¹ and Sym²r∨⊗δ: no trivial constituent in either and no κ̄⁻¹ constituent in either. The Levi adjoint part must have no κ̄⁻¹ constituent. Set χ=det(r)/δ and require D(1,1,4), for example ord(χ^bκ̄)≥5 for all |b|≤2 when χ is F_p-valued. Choose a de Rham lift of δ with weight w so that {0,a−1,w,w−a+1} are distinct, equivalently w∉{0,a−1,2a−2}. With p≫G these data give a geometric GSp₄ lift with derived Zariski-dense image.
hypotheses: All conditions depend on δ; absolute irreducibility of r alone does not imply them.
proofSteps: Use the matrix formula for both radical representations and the corrected adjoint quotient character.
Use the newform lift and a de Rham lift of δ to obtain regular local lifts of the Levi representation.
Apply maximal separation and the Levi geometric lifting theorem.
acceptance: The four Hodge–Tate weights 0,a−1,w,w−a+1 are distinct exactly when w avoids 0,a−1,2a−2 (for a≥2). The character separation depends on δ.

sources.match: The similitude-dependent exclusions and regularity restrictions repair the example.

nodes.title: Modularity of an actual residual representation
nodes.statement: For ρ̄:Γ_Q→GL₂(k), Modular(ρ̄,r,N) means that there are a normalized cuspidal newform f∈S_r(Γ₁(N)), r≥2, an embedding of its coefficient field into Q̄_p, a finite coefficient extension E containing the resulting representation, a Γ_Q-stable O_E-lattice Λ⊂E² and an embedding k_E→k̄ such that Λ/m_EΛ is isomorphic over k̄ to ρ̄. Isomorphism concerns the entire representation, including its extension class; no semisimplification is taken.
proofSteps: Use the existing newform Galois representation and stable-lattice carriers.
Quantify over coefficient extensions, integral lattices, residual embeddings and a residual intertwining isomorphism.
acceptance: An isomorphism of semisimplifications of χ⊕1 and a nonsplit extension is not a witness for actual modularity via the same lattice.

sources.match: The lattice-sensitive notion is the conclusion of Theorem 7.4 and the subject of Proposition 7.7.
