Counts all integral lattice reductions at fixed weight and level.

nodes.title: Residual hypotheses for nonsplit odd GL₂ extensions
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real, p≥3, and ρ̄ a nonsplit extension of 1 by χ̄ with χ̄(c_v)=−1 and χ̄≠κ̄⁻¹. Then C1–C4 hold. The exceptional case χ̄=κ̄ is included when it is different from κ̄⁻¹; it requires its own cocycle calculation rather than the distinct-character argument.
proofSteps: Compute the unique invariant and quotient lines of the nonsplit trace-zero adjoint representation.
Restrict to the elementary abelian p-Sylow of the finite residual splitting group and take prime-to-p quotient invariants.
Exclude most character coincidences by oddness.
For χ̄=κ̄ compute cocycle values on an F_p-basis of the unipotent p-Sylow and use the boundary map to kill the remaining one-dimensional H¹.
Use the unique adjoint quotient line to verify prime-field C3 via scalar-extension twists.
acceptance: For a split 1⊕κ̄ residual representation C4 may fail; construct a nonsplit extension before invoking the nonsplit criterion.

sources.match: This is the direct residual check that makes the p≥3 lifting theorem applicable.

nodes.title: Matching the local and global determinant
nodes.statement: For F=Q, r≥2 and the odd residual extension of 1 by χ̄, set μ=κ^{r−1}[χ̄κ̄^{1−r}]. After coefficient extension, the local ordinary potentially crystalline lift can be chosen with an unramified quotient and determinant μω, where ω has finite p-power order, trivial residual reduction and ω(Art_Qp(p))=1. Local and global Kronecker–Weber extend ω to Γ_Q, unramified away from p. At Serre weight the crystalline ordinary choice can be retained with the compatible determinant. An arbitrary unramified factor in a previously chosen quotient must be removed locally before this global extension step.
proofSteps: Use the local potentially crystalline/crystalline lift and separate its finite inertial character from its unramified quotient character.
Twist by the finite inertial normalization so ω is trivial on the chosen uniformizer.
Extend that character through Q_p× and the p-power cyclotomic extension of Q.
At the other places use the fixed-determinant local-lifting export.
acceptance: A local finite-order correction with nontrivial value on Art(p) cannot be inflated from a global character unramified outside p. The selected correction has value one there.

sources.locator: Proof of Theorem 7.4, p.36; proof of Lemma 7.2, pp.33–35
sources.match: The normalized finite character, rather than an arbitrary local unramified character, globalizes.

nodes.title: Modularity after semisimplification
nodes.statement: Every continuous odd ρ̄:Γ_Q→GL₂(k) has semisimplification isomorphic to the semisimplification of a reduction of a newform representation of some weight r≥2 and level N. In the irreducible case use Serre modularity; in the reducible case use an Eisenstein eigenform, make it cuspidal modulo p and apply Deligne–Serre lifting. This gives no control of the original extension class or a prescribed weight and level.
proofSteps: Invoke the existing Serre theorem in the irreducible case.
In the reducible case choose the Eisenstein series with the two specified residual characters.
Use an auxiliary prime or a theta iterate to make a cuspidal mod-p eigensystem, then lift it by the existing eigenform-lifting theorem.
acceptance: A nonsplit extension and the split sum have identical traces; the determinant or Hecke traces alone do not prove actual residual modularity.

sources.match: This comparison explains the extra content of actual residual modularity.

nodes.title: Modularity of reducible odd representations
nodes.statement: For p≥3 and a continuous residual representation ρ̄:Γ_{Q,S}→GL₂(k) that is an extension of 1 by χ̄ with χ̄(c)=−1 and χ̄≠κ̄⁻¹, the actual representation is modular. For every r≥2 it is modular of weight r at some level; at r=k(ρ̄|Γ_Qp), Serre’s local weight, it is modular at a level prime to p. Split extensions are included.
hypotheses: The case χ̄|Γ_Qp=1 occurs for every odd p, including p=3 (for example χ̄ the odd quadratic character of Q(√−2), trivial on Γ_Q₃ since 3 splits there, and different from κ̄⁻¹). Pan’s theorem covers it: its only p=3 exclusion is a residual character ratio equal to ω on Γ_Q₃, which does not meet χ̄|Γ_Q₃=1. No p≥5 restriction is needed.
proofSteps: For a nonsplit extension verify C1–C4 directly.
Choose the ordinary local component with the normalized determinant and desired weights; at Serre weight choose the crystalline component.
Apply the sl₂ geometric lifting theorem, ensuring irreducibility by full derived image.

Apply the exported Skinner–Wiles theorem over Q (OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.5/theorem-a-over-q: χ̄|D_p≠1, ordinary shape (∗ ∗; 0 1) on inertia, determinant ψκ^{r−1} with ψ of finite order) if χ̄|Γ_Qp≠1, and Pan’s theorem (GL2ModularityLifting R32.4/pan-residually-reducible-fontaine-mazur) if χ̄|Γ_Qp=1, for every odd p; local–global compatibility identifies weight and p-level.
For a split extension first create a nonsplit residual extension, apply the same construction and change its residual lattice to the split Levi projection.
acceptance: For a nonsplit odd extension with χ̄=κ̄⁻¹ the theorem does not apply. At Serre weight the crystalline local component gives the p-prime level conclusion.

At p=3 with χ̄ the quadratic character of Q(√−2), χ̄ is odd, trivial on Γ_Q₃ and different from κ̄⁻¹, so the theorem applies and uses the Pan case; a p≥5 restriction on that case would wrongly exclude it.

sources.match: The newform matches the full residual representation with the stated weight and level conclusions.
The residually reducible Fontaine–Mazur theorem for odd p, with its single p=3 exclusion of a cyclotomic residual ratio at 3; this is the statement of the cited supplier node.

nodes.title: The Hamblen–Ramakrishna specialization
nodes.statement: The reducible modularity theorem implies the earlier Hamblen–Ramakrishna statement for a nonsplit odd extension with χ̄≠κ̄^{±1}, χ̄²≠1, the specified nondegenerate local behavior at p and k generated by χ̄-values. These extra assumptions are unnecessary for this new conclusion. No prime-field multiplicity-freeness assertion is used.
proofSteps: Check that the older hypotheses imply p≥3, oddness and χ̄≠κ̄⁻¹.
Apply the actual modularity theorem and discard its stronger weight/level conclusions.
acceptance: A coefficient-field automorphism can repeat prime-field constituents even when the k-module is multiplicity-free; this corollary uses no false restriction-of-scalars criterion.

sources.match: The earlier statement is a logical consequence, not a second proof plan for its source.

nodes.title: The totally real conditional consequence
nodes.statement: Over a totally real F, a nonsplit odd extension of 1 by χ̄≠κ̄⁻¹ with the local ordinary μ-lifts admits the geometric irreducible lift of the sl₂ theorem. Whenever the hypotheses of the exported Skinner–Wiles theorem over F hold for that lift, it is Hilbert modular and its original integral lattice realizes the actual residual representation. This does not assert modularity over every totally real field without the modularity theorem’s extra hypotheses.
proofSteps: Apply the direct GL₂ residual criterion and choose the ordinary local components.
Construct the lift and check every hypothesis of the imported totally real modularity theorem.
Use its automorphic Galois representation comparison to retain the original residual lattice.
acceptance: If the imported totally real modularity theorem has an extra residual or local hypothesis, the implication remains conditional on it.

sources.match: The consequence is conditional on the exact available totally real modularity-lifting input.

nodes.title: Infinitely many actual extension classes
nodes.statement: Let Γ be finite, L an infinite field and χ:Γ→L×. If dim_L H¹(Γ,L(χ))>1 or dim_L H¹(Γ,L(χ⁻¹))>1, there are infinitely many pairwise nonisomorphic two-dimensional Γ-representations over L with semisimplification 1⊕χ. For χ≠1 the nonsplit classes in each orientation are projective spaces of the corresponding H¹; for χ=1 identify the two orientation copies.
proofSteps: Identify extensions of the two characters with the existing H¹ carrier.
An isomorphism between nonsplit extensions rescales the extension class, giving the projective-space quotient.
A projective line over an infinite field has infinitely many points; use an injection from it when H¹ has dimension at least two.
acceptance: For Γ=C_p, L of characteristic p and χ=1, dim H¹=1 gives a single nonzero projective class; dimension strictly greater than one is essential.

sources.match: The infinitude is over an infinite coefficient field, not the finite original k.

nodes.title: The stable-lattice segment and its reductions
nodes.statement: For an irreducible continuous ρ:Γ→GL₂(E) with residual semisimplification χ₁⊕χ₂ and χ₁≠χ₂, the homothety classes of stable O_E-lattices form a finite segment in the existing Bruhat–Tits tree. The endpoint reductions are nonsplit extensions in the two opposite orientations; interior vertices, if present, give the split representation. After any finite extension E′/E the two indecomposable reduction classes are their scalar extensions, and newly subdivided interior vertices contribute only the split class. If the residual representation is absolutely irreducible, use the existing unique-homothety theorem instead.
hypotheses: A stable lattice exists; the coefficient action is bounded and the characteristic-zero representation is irreducible.
proofSteps: Identify stable lattices with fixed vertices in the tree.
Distinct residual characters exclude branching; a fixed ray would give an invariant E-line, so the fixed segment is bounded and finite.
Analyze the neighbor quotient of a lattice to identify the two endpoints and the split interior reductions.

Choose g₀ with distinct residual eigenvalues and diagonalize it by Hensel lifting. Its integral eigenprojectors split every stable lattice, so all fixed vertices lie in one apartment. If b_g,c_g are the off-diagonal entries, Λ_s=Oe₁⊕ϖ^sOe₂ is stable precisely when −min_g v(b_g)≤s≤min_g v(c_g). Irreducibility makes both bounds finite. On extending E, the bounds multiply by the ramification index. Endpoint reductions are scalar extensions, and the new strictly interior lattices have both off-diagonal reductions zero.
acceptance: If residual characters differ, the chosen g₀ has eigenvalue difference a unit and its integral eigenprojectors split every stable lattice. Under ramification index e′ a segment of length d becomes length e′d, with the same two endpoint classes after scalar extension.

sources.locator: Proof of Proposition 7.7, p.37; Bellaïche–Chenevier (2014), Propositions 11 and 32, cited there
sources.match: This is the lattice-theoretic finiteness statement needed over the algebraic closure, beyond finite-k counting.

sources.locator: Lemma 10 and Proposition 11, pp.9–10; Definitions 29–30 and Proposition 32, pp.16–17 (author preprint pagination)
sources.match: Relates stable neighbors to residual invariant lines and bounds the fixed tree by the congruence of the two residual characters.

sources.locator: §1.2, Lemmas 1.3–1.5 and Proposition 1.4, pp.6–7; Exercises 1.5–1.9, p.8
sources.match: Gives the irreducible two-dimensional stable-segment argument and the two opposite nonsplit endpoints. Coefficient-extension invariance is supplied by the explicit matrix argument here.

nodes.title: Finitely many actual reductions at fixed weight and level
nodes.statement: Fix p odd, N≥1,r≥2 and distinct residual characters 1,χ̄ with χ̄ odd. Only finitely many isomorphism classes over k̄ of residual representations with semisimplification 1⊕χ̄ arise from stable lattices in newform representations of weight r and level N, even allowing arbitrary finite coefficient extensions and all residual embeddings. Thus a finite quotient Γ of Γ_Q with dim H¹(Γ,k̄(χ̄))>1 has infinitely many extensions of this semisimplification, only finitely many of which occur at that fixed weight and level.
proofSteps: There are finitely many normalized eigenforms and coefficient embeddings at fixed weight and level.
For each use the stable-lattice segment and extension invariance of its indecomposable endpoints.
Count the two endpoint classes and possible split class; compare with the infinite projective family.
acceptance: One newform contributes at most its two nonsplit endpoint reductions and the split class, even as its coefficient field is extended.

sources.match: The finite set remains finite after all coefficient extensions.

nodes.title: The boundary of fixed-level lifting methods
nodes.statement: For a fixed odd χ̄, one can choose a finite quotient of Γ_{Q,S} with dim H¹(Γ,k̄(χ̄))>1. The resulting infinite family with the same semisimplification cannot all be realized by modular lifts at any one fixed weight and level. Therefore a lifting argument that forces one fixed modular weight and ramification level for every member cannot prove the actual reducible modularity theorem. This is a precise obstruction to that method, not a claim that every reducible deformation ring fails a particular finiteness lemma.
proofSteps: Use controlled extension spaces and factor the finitely many chosen cocycles through one finite quotient.
Extend coefficients to k̄ and apply the projective-family infinitude.
Apply fixed-weight-and-level finiteness.
acceptance: An infinite projective extension family and a finite fixed-level set leave infinitely many classes outside that one level. This is not a claim that one uniform level realizes the family.

sources.match: The comparison states exactly the conclusion proved by the finiteness argument.

nodes.title: Actual residual automorphy over function fields
nodes.statement: For a global function field F of characteristic ℓ≠p, Automorphic(ρ̄) means that there are a cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL_n(A_F) with finite-order central character, an identification C≅Q̄_p, a finite coefficient field E, a stable O_E-lattice in its Lafforgue representation, and a residual embedding giving an isomorphism of the full lattice reduction with ρ̄ over k̄. Equivalently via the imported Langlands correspondence, ρ̄ has an integral lift that is irreducible, finitely ramified and has finite-order determinant.
proofSteps: Use the automorphic Galois representation and stable-lattice carriers from their owners.
Use both directions of the function-field Langlands equivalence, retaining the chosen lattice.
acceptance: A semisimplification isomorphism alone does not identify a nonsplit residual extension.

sources.match: The actual reduction notion parallels modularity in §7 and uses finite determinant.

api.statement: The automorphic lattice witness is equivalent to a finitely ramified irreducible integral lift with finite determinant.

The chosen residual extension or direct sum must survive the lattice construction.

nodes.title: Automorphy from the lifting hypotheses
nodes.statement: For F a global function field of characteristic ℓ≠p, p≫n and ρ̄:Γ_{F,S}→GL_n(k) satisfying C1–C4, the actual residual representation is automorphic. Choose the fixed determinant to be the Teichmüller lift of detρ̄, hence finite order. Equal-characteristic local lifts exist, and since p∤n their determinants can be corrected by an n-th root in 1+ϖO.
proofSteps: Import the equal-characteristic local lifting theorem and normalize the determinant by its unique pro-p n-th root.
Apply the global geometric lifting theorem in characteristic ℓ.
Full derived congruence image makes the characteristic-zero GL_n representation irreducible.
Apply the two-way Lafforgue correspondence and retain the integral lattice.
acceptance: The Teichmüller determinant has finite order even on constant-field Frobenius. An arbitrary p-adic determinant would not meet the stated Lafforgue contract.

sources.match: Automatic local liftability and finite determinant complete the function-field application.

nodes.title: The irreducible function-field specialization
nodes.statement: The theorem applies to an absolutely GL_n-irreducible residual representation whose restriction to Γ_{F(ζ_p)} remains absolutely irreducible and for which [F(ζ_p):F]>a_GL_n, with p≫n. Absolute irreducibility over F alone does not imply C1–C4 uniformly in F for a bound depending only on n. For fixed F a sufficient prime bound may also depend on its constant field. The stronger unramified-outside-S lifting theorem from de Jong–Gaitsgory is an independent imported result, not a consequence of this method.
proofSteps: Use the irreducible residual criteria under their actual cyclotomic hypotheses.
Apply the function-field automorphy theorem.
Check the failed uniform claim by induced two-dimensional examples over constant fields with q≡−1 mod p, where κ̄ occurs in the adjoint module.
acceptance: For F=F_q(t), q≡−1 mod p, a suitable two-dimensional representation induced from the quadratic constant extension is irreducible but has κ̄ among its adjoint constituents.

sources.locator: Remark 8.2, p.38; FKP19 Corollary A.7, pp.63–64
sources.match: The corrected comparison keeps the necessary cyclotomic conditions.

nodes.title: Automorphy for two absolutely irreducible blocks
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄ be an extension of absolutely irreducible r₂ by r₁ of dimensions n₂,n₁ over a global function field, n=n₁+n₂ and p≫n. Require r₁≄r₂ and r₁≄r₂κ̄⁻¹, and for d=gcd(n₁,n₂), χ=(det r₁)^{n₂/d}(det r₂)^{−n₁/d}, require [F(ζ_p):F(ζ_p)∩F(χ)]>b(n₁,n₂). Then ρ̄ is automorphic. For a split sum only r₁≄r₂ is needed in the second condition, since one may choose the orientation after the cyclotomic-degree check.
hypotheses: For the nonsplit case, noninjectivity of the image projection to the Levi must be proved, using complete reducibility of small finite-group representations.
proofSteps: Apply maximal separation to the primitive determinant-ratio character to obtain C3,C4.

For a nonsplit representation show that an injective image projection would force complete reducibility by the small-representation theorem; then apply the corrected maximal-parabolic criteria and the function-field theorem.
For a split sum choose an orientation avoiding the inverse-cyclotomic coincidence; both orientations cannot fail under the degree bound.
Create a nonsplit extension, lift it automorphically, and change the residual lattice to the original split sum.
acceptance: For unequal block dimensions the two Hom invariant tests vanish automatically. The primitive determinant character still has to pass its cyclotomic-degree test.

sources.match: The determinant character is primitive and the nonsplit image-projection step is explicit.

nodes.title: Automorphy of separated direct sums
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄=⊕_{i=1}^r r_i with r>1, each r_i absolutely irreducible of dimension n_i, p≫Σn_i, and r_i≄r_jψ for all i≠j and ψ∈{1,κ̄,κ̄⁻¹}. For χ_ij=(det r_i)^{n_j}(det r_j)^{−n_i}, require the joint condition [F(ζ_p):F(ζ_p)∩F(χ_ij:i≠j)]>b(n). Then ρ̄ is automorphic. gaps.title: G1 — replacement for full-family auxiliary-field independence
gaps.detail: FKP22 v5 Lemma3.7 pp.15–16 is false under its stated Assumption3.1: for F=Q, trivial SL₂ residual image and k=F_p, p≥5, M*=F_p(κ̄)³. For two basis lines, identify their scalar cocycles and put ζ_w=η_1^(w)−η_2^(w). Their equal inertia at w cancels, so ζ_w lies in the finite group H¹(Γ_{Q,T},F_p(κ̄)). Infinitely many w force ζ_w=ζ_w′ for distinct w,w′. This gives a nontrivial relation among four degree-p cocycle fields, contradicting strong disjointness. Restriction to Γ_K preserves the relation and individual nonvanishing; H¹(Gal(K/Q),F_p(κ̄))=0 as its order is p−1. C4 holds, but C1 fails. To close the main proof, establish the quantitative conditional-success/finite-quotient Chebotarev input actually needed by Proposition3.8 under C1,C3,C4, using a new construction or a proof allowing repeated constituents. Individual cyclic images or pairwise disjointness do not close it. The conditional joint-generation node is valid but its extra hypothesis is not automatic. Theorem5.2 is an intended target, not disproved by this counterexample. Independent review (REV-DESIGN-GlobalGaloisDeformationsPartII) adds that the failure also occurs under C1–C4. With k=F_p, if M* is semisimple with a simple constituent of multiplicity at least two, then for every k-basis the inertia tuple at w generates a proper F_p[Γ_F]-submodule of ∏_b M*_{e_b*}. The resulting subextension of L_w unramified at w lies in the finite maximal elementary abelian p-extension of K unramified outside T, so it repeats for two new primes. This happens for the F₄-valued examples of FKP19 Proposition 7.8 (adjoint multiplicities above one, FKP19 Remark 7.9), which satisfy C1–C4. The same diagonal-generator step recurs on p.18 of FKP22, where the fields K_{h(v)} and K_{η_b^{(v)}} are separated through ramification at t₀. So G1 is a gap in the proof of Theorem 5.2 within its hypotheses; Theorem 5.2 is not refuted, and for irreducible residual images FKP19 Theorem 6.11 has an independent proof.

gaps.detail: Several arguments use structure theory of a split reductive group in large characteristic that the current Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups layers 7–8 do not state (those layers own Borel and parabolic subgroups, Levi decompositions, root data, Bruhat decomposition and the classification) and that no atlas roadmap plans. (i) For p≫_G 0, a P-equivariant isomorphism of varieties exp: Lie U→U restricting to the ascending central series and inducing P-equivariant group isomorphisms on its graded pieces, together with the finite adjoint expansion of Ad(exp X) (FKP22 Lemma A.1, Remark A.2, p.44, and proof of Lemma A.18, p.51). (ii) Centralizers in good characteristic: smoothness of centralizers of Lie-algebra elements, containment of the centralizer of a nonzero nilpotent element in a proper parabolic, connectedness and reductivity of centralizers of semisimple elements when p is not a torsion prime, root-subgroup description of a centralizer containing a maximal torus, centralizers of tori being Levi subgroups, and generation of C_G(t) by T, root subgroups and Weyl representatives (FKP19 Lemmas A.2 and A.5, pp.61–63; FKP22 proof of Lemma A.11, pp.48–49). (iii) The G-semisimplification of a finite image: Levi projection from a minimal parabolic containing it, uniqueness up to G(k)-conjugacy, behaviour under residue-field extension, and the parabolic adjoint filtration with graded pieces m⊕u⊕u⁻ (FKP22 Lemma 6.1, p.28, and proof of Lemma A.11, p.48). (iv) Uniform finite-field root position: a root vector outside any proper F_p-subspace of g^der, and toral elements in general position with a prescribed root value (FKP19 Proposition 5.9, p.29, and Lemma 5.13, p.38). These need an owner: an atlas continuation of ReductiveGroups, or lemma nodes here if the maintainer so decides. A Tau Ceti roadmap is not extended from the atlas, so the former requests to its layers 7–8 for these inputs are withdrawn.

sourceIssues.reason: FKP22 v5 Lemma3.7 pp.15–16 is false under its stated Assumption3.1: for F=Q, trivial SL₂ residual image and k=F_p, p≥5, M*=F_p(κ̄)³. For two basis lines, identify their scalar cocycles and put ζ_w=η_1^(w)−η_2^(w). Their equal inertia at w cancels, so ζ_w lies in the finite group H¹(Γ_{Q,T},F_p(κ̄)). Infinitely many w force ζ_w=ζ_w′ for distinct w,w′. This gives a nontrivial relation among four degree-p cocycle fields, contradicting strong disjointness. Restriction to Γ_K preserves the relation and individual nonvanishing; H¹(Gal(K/Q),F_p(κ̄))=0 as its order is p−1. C4 holds, but C1 fails. To close the main proof, establish the quantitative conditional-success/finite-quotient Chebotarev input actually needed by Proposition3.8 under C1,C3,C4, using a new construction or a proof allowing repeated constituents. Individual cyclic images or pairwise disjointness do not close it. The conditional joint-generation node is valid but its extra hypothesis is not automatic. Theorem5.2 is an intended target, not disproved by this counterexample. Review addition: the lemma also fails under C1–C4 when M* is semisimple with a repeated simple constituent, for every k-basis (FKP19 Proposition 7.8 and Remark 7.9 give such residual images), so G1 concerns the proof of Theorem 5.2 within its hypotheses.
